decisions.reason: Historical Toolbox/utility library with concrete gadget wrappers. Author explicitly says file-extension reorganisation was not reflected in Makefile, so build needs repair; includes unfinished experiments and is no longer supported.

decisions.title: tj_dis Jaguar RISC disassembler
decisions.reason: Small C disassembler with Jaguar RISC opcode tables and lyxass-header detection. Must not infer 68000 from Jaguar platform: inspected instruction set targets the custom RISC processors.

decisions.title: siddasm2 SID NSF SAP disassembler
decisions.reason: Music-container-aware 6502 disassembler for SID, NSF and SAP with load/init/play entry data. Successor to Gufino's earlier SID disassembler, not a whole-game decompilation or audio decoder.

decisions.title: bhop NES music driver
decisions.reason: FamiTracker-compatible ca65 music driver with optional expansion-chip paths and banking constraints. Music data and player must be mapped during updates; channel muting integrates external sound effects rather than a complete SFX engine.

decisions.title: FamiTone 5 NES music driver
decisions.reason: Unofficial extension of Shiru's FamiTone2 with effects, full notes, volume columns and conversion tools. Requires its matching converters; fork false does not imply independent origin and it is not the original FamiTone2 project.

decisions.title: MACScnv2 X68000 animation helper
decisions.reason: Generates batch/source processing for MACS animation assets from prepared images/audio. Multi-stage workflow requires external converters, assembler/linker and modified playback stack; helper is not a standalone video decoder.

decisions.title: 86-DOS 0.11 source reconstruction
decisions.reason: Reconstructed SCP 8086 OS and utilities with original cross-assembler syntax and claimed exact binaries. Explicitly not Microsoft's official source release; old non-IBM-PC machine target and provenance are retained.

decisions.title: 86-DOS disk-image reconstruction tools
decisions.reason: Builds complete historical 86-DOS disk layouts using reconstructed source, binaries and preserved filesystem junk. Credits earlier 0.11 reconstruction; distinct image/toolchain work, not a second independent recovery of every program.

decisions.title: CoCo Audio Spectrum Analyzer disassembly
decisions.reason: Commented 1981 Steve Bjork cartridge disassembly with semigraphics, PIA/SAM addresses and kaleidoscope routines. Upstream reports working rebuild; remaining TODO/comment gaps and unverified local build are explicit.

decisions.title: Street Fighter III Third Strike PS2 decompilation
decisions.reason: Actual game AI pattern functions and data source inspected. Upstream says game code fully decompiled while CRI middleware remains partial; full-game claim must not become whole-binary completion or independent build proof.

decisions.title: Crash Team Racing native PC port
decisions.reason: Native SDL3 port based on CTR-ModSDK decompilation, with compiled game overlays and host platform layer. Retains PS1-style memory conventions but no MIPS execution requirement; requires own NTSC-U raw 2352-byte-sector disc image, not cooked ISO.

notes: Parent-only discovery across 48 platform/type searches, 327 distinct results. Forty selected repositories: 32 additions, five lineage-proven duplicates, and three documented deferrals. Five apparent new URLs were identical to or behind already tracked upstreams. Applesoft compiler-labelled skeleton only prints input bytes and has no emitter, so it was not promoted as a compiler. Empty HTTPMount and hardware-only Neo Geo board deferred. Language/platform searches generated unrelated matches; relevance was checked against pinned source rather than names. Empty README shadowed nonempty README.md for Magick2CPC, corrected during review. ResKnife fork-false mirror was checked by local commit ancestry: 9 unique modernization commits versus 13 in tracked source, so retained as a related distinct continuation rather than a duplicate or independent new editor. Native CTR game code distinguished from retained PS1 memory conventions; PS2 game-code completion distinguished from partial middleware. DOS image reconstruction credits prior source reconstruction and retained binary/junk inputs. All candidate code and media remained unexecuted; no build/runtime/exactness claims independently proven.
